key_insight: CARM prevents token-level probability changes from canceling out, giving a more reliable sequence-level mask for off-policy LLM RL updates.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical control mechanism for keeping rollout responses closer to the training policy in mathematical reasoning and code-generation systems.
method: Take the absolute value of each token log-ratio before averaging across a sampled response.
Use the resulting cancellation-aware score to decide whether the whole response is accepted for optimization.
Prove accepted responses satisfy a joint bound on out-of-band ratio mass and mean log-distance beyond the band.
evidence_signal: On math benchmarks, CARM improved mean@16 by up to 3.13 points over geometric-mean masking, and on four code benchmarks it raised average pass@1 by 2.88 points over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Because the mask is sequence-level and depends on ratio statistics, it may be sensitive to how rollout and training engines differ or to threshold/band tuning.
paper_title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
